name: docker
title: Docker
description: Creates a container per machine on one Docker host, reached over SSH or its local socket. Docker gives no network isolation: a machine can reach the LAN and the tailnet the host is on, and no egress choice is offered; the docker host's own security is yours.

permissions.detail: the Docker engine on the configured host, which is root-equivalent there: creates, starts, stops and removes containers and volumes carrying its labels, creates one network, pulls the agent image and reads engine info; nothing it makes is privileged, mounts the host or shares its namespaces
reaches the docker host over SSH as the configured user (who must be in the docker group) or through its local socket; the docker host pulls the agent image from its registry

engine.description: ssh://user@host[:port] (the user must be in the docker group, which is root on that host) or unix:///var/run/docker.sock for a plugin running on the docker host itself

ssh_private_key.description: the plugin's own key to the docker host (Generate, then add the public half to the docker user's authorized_keys); not used with a unix engine

ssh_host_key.description: the docker host's host key line (ssh-ed25519 AAAA…, or a known_hosts line); leave empty, run the check and trust the key it scanned

proxy.description: socks5://host:port the plugin reaches the docker host through (the userspace Tailscale sidecar when it runs in the pod); empty for a direct connection

bind_address.description: the docker host's IP address machines publish sshd on, and what loomuxd connects to: its tailnet IP, or 127.0.0.1 when loomuxd runs on the docker host itself

ssh_proxy.description: how loomuxd reaches the machines: default (through LOOMUX_SSH_PROXY when set) or none (directly)

agent_image.description: the image machines run, pulled by the docker host on first use; pin it by digest in production

sizes.description: machine sizes by name, each {cpu, memory, disk} in Kubernetes quantities (cpu and memory become --cpus and --memory; disk is advisory, a volume isn't capped); small/medium/large when empty

max_environments.description: how many machines this plugin makes at most; Docker has no quota beyond per-container limits, so this is the host's cap
